one: Robotics fundamentals: kinematics, statics, dynamics, planning, and control.
pos: CS 223A (ME 320) is taught by Oussama Khatib and is the classic introduction to robotics. It covers spatial transformations, forward/inverse kinematics, Jacobians and statics, dynamics, trajectory planning, and classical control, with demos on physical robot platforms/simulation.
topics: **Spatial transformations**: rotation matrices, homogeneous transforms, quaternions
**Jacobians and statics**: velocity mapping, force transmission
**Trajectories and planning**: interpolation, obstacle avoidance, RRT
assess: Assignments plus a project/exam. Check the current syllabus for details.
who: Robotics beginners; people interested in manipulation, control, or embodied AI; ME/EE/CS backgrounds all fit.
tips: Brush up on linear algebra and rigid-body transforms first. Pair with CS 225A for hands-on work.
note: Offered in Winter 2026–27; the official site is unavailable, so only the ExploreCourses link is provided.
